title: Completed finite direct image agrees with its normalized reduction tower
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0=\mathbf F_q,k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a finite morphism of separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. For a scheme $W$, write $R_W=\varprojlim_n(A_n)_W$ on the small pro-etale site $W_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Use $D^b_c(W,\mathcal O_E)$ of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], the strict derived reductions $K_n=K\otimes^L_{R_W}(A_n)_W$, and exact restriction of scalars $\operatorname{Res}_n$ [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. Let $Rf_*$ be the tower direct image of [def-weil-derived-direct-image].

Let $F_f:\operatorname{Mod}(R_X)\to\operatorname{Mod}(R_Y)$ be module direct image with the action through the canonical map $f^{-1}R_Y\to R_X$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Then $F_f$ is exact on the whole module category and preserves countable products by the canonical product comparison. It induces the termwise triangulated functor $F_{f,D}$ on ordinary derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The schemes $X,Y$ are noetherian and finite-dimensional, and $f$ is finitely presented. The same assertions hold for the finite base change $h:X\times_Ys\to s$ along any $k$-point $s=\operatorname{Spec}k\to Y$ [def-pc-base-change].

For every $K\in D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$ there is a canonical natural isomorphism in $D(\operatorname{Mod}(R_Y))$
$$\Theta_{f,K}:F_{f,D}K\xrightarrow{\sim}R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_nf_{*,n}K_n=Rf_*K.$$
Here $f_{*,n}$ is exact on all $(A_n)_X$-modules, hence is its own derived functor. With $q_n:K\to\operatorname{Res}_nK_n$ the actual reduction map and $\pi_n$ the total-limit projection, the normalization is
$$\pi_n\Theta_{f,K}=F_{f,D}(q_n),$$
using the termwise identification $F_f\operatorname{Res}_n=\operatorname{Res}_nf_{*,n}$, which identifies quotient transition maps as well. The object $Rf_*K$ is integral constructible and derived complete, and its canonical reductions $(Rf_*K)_n\to f_{*,n}K_n$ are isomorphisms. Each $K_n$ has etale origin, meaning that it is the comparison inverse image of a bounded constructible etale complex [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism, def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]. Consequently $F_{f,D}$ restricts to this integral constructible category and preserves both halves of the standard pair [def-weil-constructible-standard-tstructure].

proof.text: For a scheme of finite type over the field k, Mathlib gives a locally Noetherian source and compactness, hence IsNoetherian. Apply the finite-dimensionality bound and finite-presentation theorem to f. Finite base change makes h=pullback.snd finite; its structure map to Spec k is itself finite, hence locally of finite type and quasi-compact. The same construction therefore applies to h, including an empty source.

Apply finite_fp_proEtale_pushforward_exact to the inverse-adjoint of the actual completed coefficient map, and separately to every constant finite-coefficient direct-image map. The adjunction triangle identity identifies these with the required module direct images. Exactness makes the total right-derived unit invertible at every complex. Choose derived=sfCompletedDerivedDirectImage and factors to be the inverse cochain-unit isomorphism. Naturality of the unit proves the factorization naturality, and its inverse-hom identity is resolutionNormalization. The comparison is the identity natural isomorphism; the existing right-derived shift and triangulated instances apply.

Use the canonical pro-etale ring-module adjunction and the proved completed_direct_image_eq from SfCompleteDirectImageReduction to show that the specified underived direct image preserves products. Its scalarComparison is exactly the identity-on-sections clause of sfDirectImageRestrictionComparison_existsUnique. Exact countable products of completed module sheaves give preservation of epimorphisms by the countable product functor; descend these exact products to the derived category using derivedCategory_countableProducts_core.

The input completeness predicate already supplies the distinguished Roos triangle with its actual reduction-unit projections. The proved completed_derived_products and map_roos helpers in SfCompleteDirectImageReduction map that triangle through the specified completed derived image, using its shift and triangulated structures and its canonical product comparison. Transport the target tower along sfDerivedRestrictionComparison by roos_transport. The transition compatibility is immediate from the definition of sfDirectImageTransition, cancelling the comparison followed by its inverse. Its transported augmentation is precisely zlFiniteCompletedImageProjection, so choose its boundary from this proved triangle existence. Since comparison is the identity, normalization is Pi.lift_π. No arbitrary tower-limit object or cone comparison is chosen.

proof.text: Compute that l is a unit in k from the finite-field cardinality p^a and l!=p. Apply sfIntegralDirectImage_constructible to the just-constructed SfIntegralDirectImage, obtaining constructibility, completeness and invertibility of each actual scalar-adjoint reduction comparison. The input constructibility property gives intrinsic constructibility of each finite reduction and its common cohomological interval. The exact constant-scalar restriction carries these cohomology conditions to the fixed-module presentation. Apply the proved fixedDerivedOrigin helper of ProEtaleConstructibleOrigin and invert its resulting isomorphism to obtain the stated etaleOrigin field.

proof.text: For each degree in either standard-class vanishing range, exactness of the completed module direct image and isZero_homologyFunctor_mapDerivedCategory_obj give vanishing for the termwise derived functor. Transport this across the canonical rightDerivedFunctorIsoMapDerivedCategory to obtain vanishing for the chosen derived functor. This proves standard for both Bool values. Apply the whole field-independent finite_comparison construction to f and to each finite geometric base change h.
